quest.title: Leroy: Firing Squad
quest.description: You arranged to meet with Benoit today...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x25000, Fruity Trio x3

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Nana, Nana, would you like some fish?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Thank you, Molli. Your kindness sparkles in your lovely lavender eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Hehe, does it really? Did you really like that doll that I brought you last time?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Oh yes, yes indeed. It was very lovely. You know, I even set aside a place for it at the dining table.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Really? Oh, that would make it so happy! What about today? Do you need to lean on me during your walk? Or should I fetch your newspaper?

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: I could read it to you, too, if you can't make out the words.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Mama says that I should do one good deed every day, and my tutor wants me to submit an essay this week about good people and good things.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Oh, um... I don't mean I'm doing this because I need to write an essay, but if you don't mind, I do want to help you out.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Haha. Oh, I'm already fine, really. The best thing you could do to help me is to tell your parents that you often come by my place to play.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: I know, Mr. Leroy, and I've told them, but they don't seem too happy about it...

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Will you still come again, even so?

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: I sure will — even if they won't let me. I mean, we made an agreement, didn't we?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Haha, you are indeed a child of your word. Good, good. I do like you very much.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you two. Welcome, kind souls, welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *cough* Uh, we didn't mean to intrude or anything...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did we interrupt?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: No, no, the two of you aren't interrupting anything.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: My young friend Molli here is currently out and about, trying to complete her homework. She just happened to stop by my home.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: She'd like to do something nice for me, so that she might have some material for her essay.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Hey, I'm not helping because I want to finish my homework! Well, not just because of that, anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Of course, of course. You're not being a good child just because of your homework, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Much like these two young guests! They're not here to help me just because they need a job, either!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, well... We...

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Well now, it was just a little jest. Surely you won't begrudge an old man that much?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Youngsters have much time that they may spend freely, and you're willing to while that time away with me, and I do enjoy the company of young people... Nothing wrong with any of that, now is there?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Then perhaps I should just give you something to do. People are wont to come and go around the entrance, it tends to get dirty there very quickly, and nobody's swept behind the place for days. So, if I may ask, please help me clean it up again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... okay, then.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Molli, would you keep my cat company? Ah, and bring a fish steak if you would — her name's Nana, by the way.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: She inherited that name from a dog I had previously... It's a shame, but my daughter took her along when she went off to get married.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Alright then, Mr. Leroy.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Very well, children, off you go.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: My children aren't home, which makes cleaning the filth that gathers by the door and the back of the house quite tricky. I'm counting on you.

dialogues.speaker: Strange Boxes
dialogues.text: (Old, decrepit heavy boxes covered in layers of dust. Their presence here in the usually bright and clear Court of Fontaine is quite jarring.)

dialogues.speaker: Strange Boxes
dialogues.text: (The bases of these boxes have collected a lot of clear water stains over the years. They must have once been piled in an exceedingly damp location.)

dialogues.speaker: Strange Boxes
dialogues.text: (Never mind the stains on the door — these boxes look to be in far more urgent need of a cleanup.)

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Oh, there's no point knocking at this hour. Morticia and Athos aren't in.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: They said they'd be back today, but it seems that they've been delayed for some reason.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Ah, that's the trouble with adult children. They always have their own things to attend to, and they're often not around when you need them.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Are you all done?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, the cleanup's done, and Molli's fed the cat, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, Benoit, there's a pile of super dirty old boxes next to your place. Do you want us to clean those up, too?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Oh, those boxes? I just store some old stuff in them... Otherwise, they don't see much use.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Some of them contain furniture and other small items from my old place, which I haven't had the heart to throw away... But at the same time, they don't fit with my current home, and so, they've ended up just stacked out there.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: I don't touch them for the most part, but since everyone around here's a decent sort, no one's stolen anything — so they can stay right where they are.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Mr. Leroy, Mr. Leroy, was I helpful?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Why, of course you were, Molli. Don't forget to say hello to your parents for me. I'd be even more grateful if you could do that.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: And I've got the snacks and pocket money right here, children, so come and get it.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Oh, no, no, I don't need any pocket money. I'd just like to pet Nana some more. Can I?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Oh, of course, please do, but watch out for her claws, and remember to come back for snacks once you're done playing.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Why did you go out, Dad?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Well, this old fellow got lonely, what with his children not being around to keep him company and all — so he decided to go get some fresh air.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Ah, Morticia, would you look at that — gone but a few days, and he's mad at us already.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: But I'm sure he'd forgive us if he only knew what gift we'd brought back this time, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Gift? What did you bring back?

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Something wonderful, of course. You'll know when you see it. Morticia knows how you like lovely, expensive things. She picked it out especially for you.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Thank you, my daughter.

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: I did only what I should have.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. These two lovely guests are also children who came by to play while the two of you were out.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Hello there. My father's a friendly man and really loves kids, so thank you for keeping him company, truly.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Still, since my wife and I are back, we'll take it from here.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Ah, it really is good that you're back. Come now, let me have a look at that present.

dialogues.speaker: Morticia
dialogues.text: Alright, Dad. Let's go inside, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Indeed, indeed. Athos, do remember to give them their pay and some snacks. They helped me sweep the place, and fed Nana, too.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Ah, and give that young lady some of those treats, too, would you? I'm going back inside now.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Mr. Leroy, Nana let me give her a belly rub... Eh? Where's he gone?

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Are you looking for my father, little lady? I'm his son-in-law... Well, you might as well just consider me his son to keep things simple. Call me Athos.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Oh, I know what a son-in-law is. That means you're his daughter's husband.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Haha, you sure are knowledgeable, aren't you? Thanks for keeping my father company — he's gone indoors.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: These snacks are for you. You can leave the rest to my wife and I — it's alright if you don't drop by anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Anyway, you should head home soon. Your family will be worried about you if you're out too long.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry, Mister. It was no trouble at all, and anyway, Mr. Leroy and I have an agreement.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: I think he might need my help going forward, too — you know, with feeding the cat, watering plants, and other stuff. Helping people makes me happy, too, so I'll definitely come back!

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Tch. And that's what makes things tricky.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Um, is something wrong, Mister?

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: No, little lady, not at all. I have something important to discuss with you... Hmm, no. Discussion isn't the right word. There's something I need you to do.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Sure. What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: I'm going to give you the snacks and pocket money, and then after that, don't come back again, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Huh? Why? Did I do something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: No, of course you haven't! It's just that my father's health has always been poor, and his insomnia has gotten quite bad lately.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Out of consideration for his health, my wife and I would like him to have an environment conducive to rest. You understand, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Oh, so Mr. Leroy's unwell... I get it. Next time, I'll bring extra Bulle Fruit.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Every time I eat too much cake and get a tummy ache, Papa tells me I should eat less sweets and have more fruit.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: As long as Mr. Leroy eats some fruit every day, he'll be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* Nevermind. Nothing else for it.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: As for you two, here are your snacks and rewards.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: And now, let me speak plainly.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: I am speaking for the entire Leroy family on this matter: I hope that you will not come and disturb us again in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: I believe that despite your youth, you will be able to understand my meaning. So please, do not go out of your way to return here.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: That's all. I'll take my leave now.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Huh. Why can't we come back? It's so weird! Mr. Leroy was so nice, but this man just really doesn't want us to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! This guy speaks politely enough, alright, but he's as cold as they come.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Well, I don't care what he says. I'm going to come see Mr. Leroy tomorrow. What about you two?

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Come on, just come along. Nana's so cute, and I just wanna pet her a bit more... and also, Mr. Leroy's going to give us more snacks.

choices.text: Last one to show is a rotten egg!

response.speaker: Molli
response.text: Alright, no takesies-backsies, 'kay? We've gotta come pet the cat and play with Mr. Leroy.

response.speaker: Molli
response.text: Alright. See you next time, then.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Newspaper delivery? Just leave it by the door, thanks. I'll come get it later.

dialogues.speaker: Door
dialogues.text: (You've already helped Benoit out today. It would be rude to disturb his rest. You agreed to meet him tomorrow, so it'd be best to just do that.)
